messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — rollback observability & sanity checks for on‑prem / air‑gapped upgrades. Updated proposal here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/onprem-rollback-observability (TL;DR: add agent-side activation telemetry, manifest preflight dry-run, short-lived recovery tokens, and a conservative auto-rollback policy). Looking for edge-case gaps: partial apply, powercut mid-apply, and operator UX for manual rollbacks.

drew: big +1 for recovery tokens. question: where should we persist them? local sealed storage on the node or central verifier? :thinking:

maya: prefer embedding a signed, short‑TTL recovery token inside the sealed manifest bundle. token only usable when operator explicitly requests rollback; issuance recorded in audit log and manifests carry the token fingerprint. avoids central availability dependency in air‑gapped setups.

charlie: we need richer agent status signals — applied step index, per-component hashes, and healthchecks after each stage. sample status payload:
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "r-3425",
  "applied_index": "42",
  "component_hashes": ["sha256:aa...", "sha256:bb..."],
  "health": "pass",
  "uptime_secs": "120"
}
```
This lets the controller reason about partial applies and detect drift.

leah: note: logs + full hashes are heavy in air‑gapped envs. propose we also emit a compressed diff summary and a bloom filter of changed file paths to keep diagnostics compact.

samir: ops playbook thought: if an agent reports STALLED for > X minutes, mark it stale. auto-rollback if >50% of nodes in a replica set fail healthchecks AND there is zero progress for 15m. question: are we ok with automatic rollback or should it always require operator confirm?

maya: propose conservative auto-rollback for >50% failures + no progress for 15m to avoid prolonged downtime. operator confirmation still required for cross-region rollbacks. Canary boolean allowed to enable partial rollouts without auto-rollback during early tests. :thumbsup:

charlie: integration idea — tag all requests with rollout_id and surface events in Redwood Console traces. adds visibility for distributed failure modes and lets SRE correlate request failures to rollout windows.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary test started on env-staging with rollout-id r-3425; nodes=2; status=healthy.

maya: next steps: I'll update the RFC with (1) agent status schema, (2) recovery-token lifecycle, (3) audit event definitions, and (4) CLI operator commands (issue/revoke/inspect). @drew @charlie can you own the agent status schema? @leah @samir can you draft playbook thresholds and compressed diagnostics format?

drew: taking agent schema. will drop a proto sketch by EOD.

samir: I'll write the playbook and include thresholds + escalation steps. quick q: we should keep previous images/artifacts around for fast rollback — how many generations?

maya: keep previous N=2 images/artifacts by default, allow operator to configure N up to 5. ensure compact diff cache so retention cost stays small. Also add a CLI command: `rw rollback --rollout r-XYZ --force` that validates recovery token fingerprint before performing the revert.

charlie: one more edge-case: partial image swap where agent applied blobs but didn't activate. we should surface a `pending_activation` flag in status and allow remote activation after verifying file hashes.

leah: noted — I'll add the bloom-filter + compressed-diff proto to the diagnostics doc.

maya: great — thanks all. will push RFC update and tag you for review. :rocket:
